questions.question: The central bank may ________ to discourage credit in the economy.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**increase bank rate.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__ Key Points__**

__
 
• **The bank rate** is the interest rate at which the central bank **lends money** to commercial banks.
 
• When the central bank** increases the bank rate**, it becomes **more expensive** for commercial banks to borrow money from the central bank.
 
• This, in turn,** reduces** the amount of credit that commercial banks can offer to their customers, thereby **discouraging credit** in the economy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Increasing **the Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR) is another tool that the central bank can use to** discourage credit.**

 
 
• **CRR **is the amount of funds that commercial banks have to keep with the central bank as a** percentage of their deposits**.
 
• When the **CRR is decreased**, banks have more funds available to lend, which can lead to an** increase in credit** in the economy.
 
 
 
• **Buying securities** in the open market is a tool that the central bank can use to **increase liquidity** in the economy.
 
 
• When the central bank buys securities, it i**njects money** into the economy, which can lead to an** increase in credit.**
 
• Therefore, this option is** not** suitable for discouraging credit in the economy.
 
 
 
• **Reducing** the **Statutory Liquidity Ratio** (SLR) is another tool that the central bank can use to **increase the availability of funds** for banks to lend.
 
 
• SLR is the percentage of deposits that banks have to keep in the form of liquid assets such as** cash, gold, or government securities.**
 
• When the SLR is** reduced**, banks have** more funds available** to lend, which can lead to an increase in credit in the economy.

questions.question: Which of the following does NOT come under the Fundamental Duties in the Constitution of India?

options.text: Safeguard public property and to abjure violence
Cherish and follow the noble ideals that inspired the national struggle for freedom
Uphold and protect the sovereignty, unity and integrity of India

questions.solution:
The correct answer is the __**Exercise adult franchise.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The** Fundamental Duties** are enshrined in **Part IV-A **of the Constitution and were added by the **42nd Amendment in 1976.**
 
• There are **11 Fundamental Duties** listed in** Article 51-A,** which are **non-justiciable **in nature, meaning that they **cannot be enforced** by law.
 
• The exercise of the adult franchise is** not** a Fundamental Duty, but rather a Right given to citizens under **Article 326** of the Constitution.
 
• **51(A)(a)**: Abide by the Constitution, respect its ideals, the National Flag, and the National Anthem.
 
• **51(A)(b):** Cherish and follow ideals from the national struggle for freedom.
 
• **51(A)(c):** Uphold the sovereignty, unity, and integrity of India.
 
• **51(A)(d): **Defend the country and render national service when required.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Exercise adult franchise **refers to the **right to vote** in elections, which is a key feature of a **democratic system.**
 
• **Safeguarding public property and abjuring violence** is important for maintaining **law and order** in the country.
 
• **Cherishing and following the noble ideals that inspired the national struggle for freedom** is a way of paying **homage to the leaders** and movements that fought for India's independence.
 
• **Upholding and protecting the sovereignty, unity, and integrity of India** is crucial for maintaining **national security and preventing any threats** to the country's territorial integrity.

questions.question: Which festival has the meaning 'to boil' or 'boiling' in its name?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Pongal**.

__
 
• The festival with the meaning '**to boil**' or **'boiling'** in its name is Pongal.
 
• Pongal is a harvest festival celebrated in the southern Indian state of **Tamil Nadu**.
 
• The festival is named after the dish 'Pongal', which is made by boiling rice and lentils together with milk and jaggery.
 
• Pongal is celebrated for four days and is a time for thanksgiving to the sun god for a bountiful harvest.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Vamana** and the magnanimous daitya ruler Mahabali are remembered on Onam.
 
 
 
• **Raja** is a festival celebrated in the eastern Indian state of **Odisha**.
 
 
• The festival's second day marks the start of the solar month of Mithuna, which is when the rainy season begins.
 
 
 
• **Bihu** is a festival celebrated in the northeastern Indian state of **Assam**.
 
 
• Every Bihu falls on a unique day in the agricultural calendar.
 
• The Bohag Bihu heralds the beginning of the seeding season, the Kati Bihu the end of the paddies' sowing and transplanting, and the Magh Bihu the conclusion of the harvesting season.

i - c, ii - a, iii - b, iv - d

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**i - c, ii - d, iii - b, iv - a.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The correct match is **i - c, ii - d, iii - b, iv - a.**__
 
• **Electric current** is the flow of electric charge while **Ampere** is the unit to measure the electric current.
 
• **Voltage** is the electric potential difference between two points while** Volt** is the unit to measure the voltage.
 
• **Capacitance** is the ability of a body to store an electric charge while **Farad** is the unit to measure the capacitance.
 
• **Magnetic field** is a field that surrounds a magnetic material or a moving electric charge while **Tesla** is the unit to measure the magnetic field.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• A** unit of measurement **is a specific amount of a quantity that is used as a benchmark for **measuring other quantities **of the same kind.
 
• It can be established and adopted by **legislation or agreement.**
 
• It is possible to express any other quantity of that type as a **multiple of the measurement unit.**
 
• A** length**, for instance, is a physical quantity.
 
• The** metric system** that is widely used as a benchmark for measurements is the **International System of Units** (SI).

• Ashoka was coronated in **268 BCE **and he conquered** Kalinga in 261 BCE.**
 
• Kalinga was a powerful kingdom in **eastern India **and Ashoka's conquest of it was a turning point in his life.
 
• The brutal war and its aftermath made Ashoka realize the futility of **violence** and he embraced **Buddhism**, becoming a champion of peace and non-violence.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• Its borders have changed with the territory of its rulers, but generally speaking, it is classified as the **eastern coastal region** between the **Mahanadi** and **Godavari **rivers.
 
• Presently, the entirety of **Odisha** and a small portion of northern **Andhra Pradesh** make up the main territory of Kalinga.
 
• The **Suryavamsa Gajapatis**, the **Bhoi **dynasty, the **Paralakhemundi Gangas**, and the **zamindaris of Ganjam **and **Vizagapatam **were the medieval-age kings who ruled over the Kalinga region.

questions.question: Who is known as the 'Father of Modern Dance in India'?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Uday Shankar.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Uday Shankar** is known as the **Father of Modern Dance** in India for his contributions to the development of modern dance in the country.
 
• He was a pioneer in incorporating Indian **classical dance** forms with **Western dance styles**, creating a unique and innovative style of dance.
 
• Uday Shankar also established the first Indian dance school, the **Uday Shankar India Culture Centre,** in **Almora, Uttarakhand.**
 
• He is also known for his collaborations with famous artists such as **Pablo Picasso** and **Igor Stravinsky.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Birju Maharaj** is a famous **Kathak dancer** and choreographer, known for his contributions to the classical dance form.

 
 
• He performed Kathak dance as an exponent of the Lucknow **"Kalka-Bindadin" Gharana** in India. 
 
 
 
• **Gopi Krishna** was a **Kathak dancer and choreographer**, as well as a **spiritual teacher **and **author.**
 
 
• He learned **Bharatnatyam** as well.
 
 
 
• **Guru Bipin Singh** was a **Manipuri dancer **and choreographer, known for his contributions to the classical dance form.
 
 
• He founded the **Manipuri Nartanalaya dance school** in **Calcutta in 1972** as well as the **Govindji Nartanalaya dance school **for women in Imphal.

questions.question: Who was the first nationalist to give the theory of the drain of wealth from India to England?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Dadabhai Naoroji.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Dadabhai Naoroji** was the **first nationalist leader **who gave the **theory of the drain of wealth** from **India to England.**
 
• He was a** Parsi intellectual **and a **social reformer **who was also known as the **"Grand Old Man of India".**
 
• Naoroji wrote a book in **1867 **titled **"Poverty and Un-British Rule in India"** in which he explained how **British colonialism** was exploiting India's resources and draining its wealth.
 
• He estimated that India was losing around** 200-300 million pounds** annually to Britain due to various economic** policies and practices**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mahatma Gandhi** was a prominent leader in **India's freedom struggle** who advocated for **non-violent civil disobedience **and** mass movements** to achieve independence.

 
 
• After taking over as the **Indian National Congress's leader in 1921**, Gandhi oversaw national campaigns to abolish** untouchability**, promote **women's rights, **reduce **poverty**, foster **interethnic and religious harmony,** and, most importantly, achieve **swaraj, or self-rule**. 
 
 
 
• **RC Dutt** was an Indian** civil servant, economist, and writer** who wrote extensively on India's **economic and social **conditions during the colonial period.
 
 
• He translated the **Mahabharata and the Ramayana.**
 
 
 
• **SN Banerjee **was a** lawyer and politician** who was one of the founders of the Indian National Congress and played a key role in the **Swadeshi movement **against British goods.
 
 
• To unite **Muslims and Hindus **for political action, Banerjee established the **Indian National Association**, a nationalist group. 
 
 
 
• The theory of **drain of wealth** became a key concept in India's nationalist discourse and was used to highlight the economic exploitation of India by British colonialism.

questions.question: During Alauddin Khilji's reign, the cloth market was known as ________.
questions.solution:

__
 
• During **Alauddin Khilji's** reign, the cloth market was known as **Sarai-i-Adl.**
 
• Sarai-i-Adl was a market established by Alauddin Khilji to regulate the** trade of cloth** and **prevent fraudulent practices.**
 
• The market was located in** Delhi** and was known for its strict regulations and fair prices.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mandi** is a term used for a market or a place where** goods are sold.**
 
• Every vendor had an account with the **Market division.**
 
 
• The Sultan received reports from the **munhiyans**, a clandestine group of spies, on how these markets were operating.
 
 
 
• During Alauddin Khilji's reign, the entire grain market was referred to as **Shahna I Mandi.**
 
 
• Alauddin had appointed **Malik Qabul**, who used to ride his horse and a few slaves to the marketplaces, to **oversee **all of the grain markets.

questions.question: The Ryotwari Settlement, in which cultivators had to pay annual taxes directly to the government, was primarily introduced in which of the following provinces?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Madras and Bombay.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Ryotwari Settlement **was introduced in **Madras and Bombay** provinces during the British rule in India.
 
• Under this system, cultivators or farmers had to pay annual taxes directly to the government, unlike the **Zamindari system** where they paid taxes to intermediaries or landlords.
 
• The Ryotwari system was considered more beneficial for **small and marginal farmers** as they had direct access to the government and could negotiate the amount of taxes based on their **produce and income**.
 
• The system also helped in **increasing agricultural productivity** and **revenue** for the government.
 
• However, the system was criticized for being exploitative towards farmers in some cases, especially during **famines and crop failures.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Central province **was mainly governed under the** Zamindari system**, where intermediaries collected taxes from farmers and paid a** fixed amount** to the government.
 
• **Assam and Bengal **provinces had a mix of** Zamindari and Mahalwari systems, **where taxes were collected either by intermediaries or directly from farmers through **village-level committees.**
 
• **Punjab **province had a predominantly **Mahalwari system**, where large landlords or Zamindars **collected taxes from farmers** and paid a fixed amount to the government.

questions.question: In which part of the Himalayas does its highest mountain peak, Kanchenjunga, lie?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The Darjeeling and Sikkim Himalayas.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Kanchenjunga**, the highest mountain peak in the Himalayas, lies in the** Darjeeling **and **Sikkim** Himalayas.
 
• The Darjeeling and Sikkim Himalayas are located in the** eastern part** of the Himalayan range.
 
• Kanchenjunga is the** third highest mountain peak** in the world with an elevation of **8,586 meters **(28,169 feet).
 
• The Kanchenjunga mountain range is located on the border between **India and Nepal.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Arunachal Himalayas** are located in the** easternmost part** of the Himalayan range and are home to many peaks over** 7,000 meters **in height.

 
 
• The Arunachal Himalayas stretch from the **Diphu Pass **in the east to the **eastern Himalayas of Bhutan.**
 
 
 
• The **Kashmir Himalayas** are located in the northernmost part of the Himalayan range and are known for their **scenic beauty and ski resorts.**
 
 
• The ranges that comprise this area are the **Pir Panjal, Zanskar, Ladakh, and Karakoram.**
 
 
 
• The **Uttarakhand Himalayas** are located in the central part of the Himalayan range and are home to many famous peaks, including **Nanda Devi and Kamet.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

questions.question: In the early 1800s, who discovered that each chemical element is made up of a unique type of atom and that atoms differ by their mass?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**John Dalton.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **John Dalton** discovered that each chemical element is made up of a **unique type of atom **and that atoms **differ by their mass **in the early 1800s.
 
• Dalton proposed the **atomic theory** which explained the **behavior of atoms** and their interactions with other atoms.
 
• **Dalton's atomic theory** also stated that atoms **cannot be created or destroyed** in a chemical reaction and that compounds are formed by the combination of **atoms in fixed ratios.**
 
• Dalton's work laid the foundation for **modern atomic theory **and the** periodic table** of elements.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Antoine Lavoisier **is known as the **father of modern chemistry.**

 
 
• He made significant contributions to the understanding of **combustion** and the **law of conservation of mass.**
 
 
 
• **Amedeo Avogadro **proposed **Avogadro's law.**
 
 
• The law states that **equal volumes of gases** at the **same temperatur**e and **pressure** contain equal numbers of molecules.
 
 
 
• **Robert Boyle** is known for **Boyle's law.**
 
 
• The law states that the volume of a gas is **inversely proportional** to its pressure at a constant temperature.

questions.solution:

__
 
• **Addison's **disease is caused due to **adrenal gland disorder.**
 
• **Hashimoto's** disease is caused due to** thyroid gland **disorder.
 
• **Acromegaly **is caused due to **growth hormone disorder**.
 
• **SIADH **is caused due to **vasopressin disorder.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Addison's disease** is a rare disorder that occurs when adrenal glands **do not produce** enough hormones, causing** fatigue, weight loss, and low blood pressure.**
 
• **Hashimoto's **disease is an **autoimmune **disorder that affects the** thyroid gland**, causing an underactive thyroid gland, leading to weight gain, fatigue, and depression.
 
• **Acromegaly** is a hormonal disorder that occurs when the **pituitary gland produces **too much growth hormone, causing enlargement of hands, feet, and facial features.
 
• **SIADH** is a disorder that occurs when the body produces too much **vasopressin hormone**, leading to fluid retention and low sodium levels in the blood.
 
• **Hormones and glands** play a crucial role in regulating various** bodily functions,** and any disorder related to them can cause significant **health issues.**

questions.question: Which of the following sedimentary minerals, known to everyone as 'salt', usually form in arid climates where seawater evaporates?
questions.solution:

__
 
• **Halite** is a **sedimentary mineral** that forms in arid climates where **seawater evaporates,** leaving behind **salt deposits.**
 
• Halite is also known as **rock salt** and is commonly used as a **seasoning or preservative** in food.
 
• Halite forms** isometric crystals.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• They are mostly made of **silicon, aluminum, and oxygen.**
 
 
 
• **Calcite** is a mineral that is used in the production of **cement, lime, **and as a building stone.
 
 
• Based on a comparison of **scratch hardness,** calcite is classified as having a** hardness of 3** on the Mohs mineral hardness scale. 
 
 
 
• **Pyrite **is a mineral that is commonly known as** fool's gold **and is often mistaken for gold due to its** metallic luster,** but it has no economic value.
 
 
• The most common sulfide mineral is **pyrite.**

questions.question:
Which of the following modern industries was in operation in India during British rule?

a. Cotton

b. Jute

c. Iron and Steel

options.text: All of a, b and c

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**All of a, b, and c.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Cotton, jute, and iron and steel** were all modern industries that were in operation in** India** during British rule.
 
• **Cotton **was one of the most important industries during this time, with India being one of the** largest cotton producers** in the world.
 
• The British established** cotton mills** in India to process the **raw cotton** and **export the finished products** back to Britain.
 
• **Jute** was another important industry, with India being the **largest producer** of jute in the world.
 
• Jute mills were established in** Bengal **to process the raw jute and export the finished products.
 
• **Iron and steel production** also began to develop in India during the British rule.
 
• The Tata Iron and Steel Company was established in** 1907** and became one of the** largest steel producers** in the world.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Other modern industries that developed during British time included** tea production, mining, and railway construction.**
 
• By building the** third-largest railroad network** in the world, the British brought India together and made it possible for it to develop a modern economy.
 
• India was able to modernize thanks to the construction of **telephone and telegraph lines, road networks, irrigation systems, dams, bridges, and canals.**
 
• The founding of the cotton textile industry in **Bombay in 1854** marked the beginning of India's modern industrial sector in an organized manner.

questions.question: Which of the following ports is NOT situated on the west coast of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Haldia.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Haldia port** is situated on the **east coast **of India, in the state of **West Bengal,** and not on the west coast.
 
• **Mangaluru port** is situated on the** west coast **of India, in the state of **Karnataka.**
 
• **Kandla Port** is situated on the **west coast** of India, in the state of **Gujarat.**
 
• **Marmagao port** is situated on the west coast of India, in the state of **Goa.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The west coast of India is a major hub for** maritime trade and transportation**, with several important ports located along its coastline.
 
• These ports serve as gateways for the** movement of goods and commodities** between India and other countries.
 
• Mangaluru port is a major port in Karnataka, handling a variety of cargo such as** crude oil, petroleum products, coal, fertilizers, and timber.**
 
• Kandla Port is one of the largest ports in India and is known for its container **terminals, dry docks, and liquid cargo handling facilities.**
 
• Marmagao port is a natural harbor located in Goa and is primarily used for the export of **iron ore, manganese ore, and bauxite.**
 
• Haldia port, on the other hand, is situated on the east coast of India and is primarily used for the handling of bulk cargo such as **coal, iron ore, and petroleum products.**
